newsitem.title: INDIA: Criminal Sobhraj deported to France from India.
newsitem.headline: Criminal Sobhraj deported to France from India.

text.p: Notorious criminal Charles Sobhraj on Monday bid adieu to years of imprisonment in India and headed for a free life in France where he said he would feel "like a stranger".
"I am going to feel like a stranger in Paris," he told reporters minutes before he entered the Indira Gandhi International Airport in New Delhi to catch a flight to France.
Sobhraj, who was born to an Indian father and Vietnamese mother and claims French citizenship, served 20 years in an Indian jail on a string of charges including murder and robbery.
"He is being deported to France on an Air France flight scheduled to leave for France at 00:30 a.m. (1900 GMT)," his lawyer Rajan Bakshi told Reuters.

Sobhraj plans to concentrate on working on a $15 million English-language film based on his life, to be produced in France with American actors. He said he would write the script but would not play the title role.
Sobhraj, whose criminal exploits across Asia have been the subject of two books, was philosophical about his departure. "I have no choice," he said.

India ordered Sobhraj's deportation in February but France refused to accept him pending checks on his past record and nationality claim. France agreed on Monday that Sobhraj had a strong and legitimate claim for French citizenship.

"Our checks have enabled us to dispel doubts about Mr Sobhraj's nationality," French Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said in Paris. "We have very strong reasons to believe that his nationality is French."
Doutriaux said Sobhraj would have to apply for a certificate of citizenship, but indicated it would be a formality.
"It will be up to him to apply for a certificate of French nationality that will be granted by a judge," he said.
Bakshi said two officials of the Foreigners' Regional Registration Office (FRRO) would accompany his client to Paris and hand him over to the French authorities.
"He will be handed over his ticket and the travel documents at the airport itself," Bakshi said.
Sobhraj, wearing a dark blue blazer and grey trousers, told reporters that he was optimistic about his return to India.
"I will definitely come back," he said. Sobhraj has two half-sisters in India.

Sobhraj was first arrested in India for holding up a hotel jewellery shop in 1971. He was later charged with a long string of crimes including murder, serving time for some and winning acquittal in others.
He had said that once set free he would like to roam the streets of Paris to enjoy his freedom. "I want to take a walk on the bank of the River Seine in Paris," he said.
